question: How do the MUTCD headings Standard, Guidance, Option, and Support differ, including the verbs typically associated with them?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD defines its four text headings in Section 1C.01. A Standard is a required, mandatory, or specifically prohibitive practice (typically using "shall"); Guidance is a recommended practice in typical situations (typically using "should") from which deviations are allowed with engineering judgment or study; an Option is a permissive condition carrying no requirement or recommendation (associated with "may"), and may modify Standard or Guidance statements. The evidence provided is cut off before the full definition of Support, but Support statements are non-normative headings distinct from the other three categories. Standards (mandatory): - "When used in this Manual, the text headings of Standard, Guidance, Option, and Support shall be defined as follows: A. Standard-a statement of required, mandatory, or specifically prohibitive practice regarding a traffic control device. In limited, location-specific cases, the results of a documented engineering study (see Section 1D.03) might indicate a deviation from one or more requirements of a Standard provision to be appropriate. All Standard statements are labeled, and the text appears in bold type. The verb 'shall' is typically used. The verbs 'should' and 'may' are not used in Standard statements. Standard statements are sometimes modified by Option statements." - "B. Guidance-a statement of recommended practice in typical situations, with deviations allowed if engineering judgment or engineering study (see Section 1D.03) indicates the deviation to be appropriate. All Guidance statements are labeled, and the text appears in unbold italic type. The verb 'should' is typically used. The verbs 'shall' and 'may' are not used in Guidance statements. Guidance statements are sometimes modified by Option statements." - "C. Option-a statement of practice that is a permissive condition and carries no requirement or recommendation. Option statements sometimes contain allowable modifications to a Standard or Guidance statement. All Option statements are labeled..." Guidance (recommended): - (None in the evidence directly addressing the heading definitions.) Options (permitted): - (None in the evidence directly addressing the heading definitions.) Note on Support: The supplied text of Section 1C.01 is truncated before the definition of the Support heading, so its full official definition cannot be quoted here. However, Section 6P.01 illustrates that notes in typical application diagrams are "clearly classified using headings as being Standard, Guidance, Option, or Support," confirming Support is a distinct, labeled category alongside the three normative ones. Citations: - Section 1C.01 Standard §1 (p.13) - Section 6P.01 Support §2 (p.857)
gold_answer: A Standard is mandatory or prohibitive and typically uses 'shall.' Guidance is recommended practice with justified deviations allowed and typically uses 'should.' An Option is permissive and typically uses 'may.' Support is informational and conveys no mandate, recommendation, permission, prohibition, or enforceable condition.
